matches.rationale: GT1 says the swap-of-Hodge-components construction underlying Theorem 2.3 only yields actual complex conjugation when the Hodge piece is 1-dimensional, i.e. the stated map in the proof is not literally complex conjugation without an added conjugate. Finding 2 catches this directly by showing the theorem's displayed equation equates classes in conjugate Hodge types without a conjugate bar, which is logically impossible unless both sides vanish — exactly the symptom of the swap not being true conjugation. Finding 9 flags the same root issue elsewhere in the same proof (the pairing C and the inverse map both silently drop a required conjugate), corroborating that the construction systematically omits the conjugation needed for correctness.
